evidence.claim: The Lake Mille Lacs Scenic Byway circles the lake on 68 paved miles, with lake views and communities along the way.
evidence.quote: Setting: Lake views and local communities Surface: Paved Suitable Vehicle: Any vehicle Length: 68 miles

evidence.claim: The byway organization allows 1.5 to 2 hours for the drive.
evidence.quote: Time: 1.5 to 2 hours

evidence.claim: Explore Minnesota identifies it as the state’s 22nd byway and highlights wildlife viewing, state parks, Civilian Conservation Corps sites and the Mille Lacs Indian Museum and Trading Post.
evidence.quote: The Lake Mille Lacs 68-mile Scenic Byway is the state’s 22nd byway.

evidence.claim: highlights wildlife viewing, state parks, Civilian Conservation Corps sites and the Mille Lacs Indian Museum and Trading Post.
evidence.quote: birding and wildlife viewing, the Mille Lacs Indian Museum and Trading Post in Vineland, several historic Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) camp sites from the 1930s and 1940s, the nations smallest national wildlife refuge and two State Parks.

evidence.claim: The western shore’s motoring history began before this loop: a scenic highway was designated there in 1917, and the road became U.S. 169 in 1931.
evidence.quote: a scenic highway was designated along its western shore in 1917

evidence.claim: the road became U.S. 169 in 1931.
evidence.quote: The road became U.S. Route 169 in 1931.

evidence.claim: During the Depression, the Minnesota Highway Department used New Deal funds and labor to realign roads and create waysides for motorists.
evidence.quote: In the 1930s the Minnesota Highway Department began an ambitious series of improvement projects to realign roadways and establish scenic waysides, taking advantage of federal funds and labor provided by the New Deal to combat the Great Depression.

evidence.claim: Civilian Conservation Corps workers built the Garrison Concourse between 1936 and 1939, part of a larger lakeshore parkway project.
evidence.quote: It was built from 1936 to 1939 as the centerpiece of the Mille Lacs Highway Development Plan, a major New Deal project to create a scenic parkway along the lakeshore.

evidence.claim: Civilian Conservation Corps workers built the Garrison Concourse
evidence.quote: During the summer of 1936 the Civilian Conservation Corps enrollees built a cofferdam to hold back the lakewater and laid the footings of the overlook wall.

evidence.claim: Near Garrison, the same camp widened ten miles of highway from two lanes to four and built four stone-faced bridges. The work fell short of the original ambition for a scenic highway all the way round the lake.
evidence.quote: Camp SP-15 widened the highway from two lanes to four for 10 miles (16 km), realigned a section, constructed two other wayside rests and four stone-faced bridges, and landscaped the right-of-way.  This fell far short of the original hope to develop a scenic highway all the way around the lake

evidence.claim: Nineteen identified archaeological sites lie within Mille Lacs Kathio State Park.
evidence.quote: The park contains 19 identified archaeological sites

evidence.claim: The earliest dates to the Archaic period and contains evidence of copper tool manufacture.
evidence.quote: The earliest site dates to the Archaic period and shows evidence of copper tool manufacture.

evidence.claim: Preserved habitation sites and mound groups document Dakota culture and Ojibwe-Dakota relationships.
evidence.quote: The park preserves habitation sites and mound groups, believed to date between 3000 BC and 1750 AD, that document Dakota Indian culture and Ojibwe-Dakota relationships.

evidence.claim: Later, logging changed the landscape: trees felled over the half-century after the 1850s were floated down the Rum River or across Mille Lacs Lake to sawmills.
evidence.quote: The next 50 years resulted in a large quantity of trees being felled and floated down the Rum River or across Mille Lacs Lake to sawmills.

evidence.claim: after the 1850s
evidence.quote: Around the time of contact in the 1850s, loggers came to the area.

evidence.claim: The Kathio Historic District became a National Historic Landmark in 1964.
evidence.quote: The Kathio Historic District site was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1964.

evidence.claim: The park also has an observation tower to climb, with hiking, biking and camping among its other visitor activities.
evidence.quote: Climb the Observation Tower at Kathio, put your toes in the sand at the Father Hennepin State Park beach, hike, bike, camp and enjoy the great outdoors in both locations.

evidence.claim: The Four Seasons Room follows an Ojibwe year through life-size dioramas made in 1964.
evidence.quote: The room features life-size dioramas, made in 1964, that depict traditional Ojibwe activities.

evidence.claim: Summer berry picking leads to fall wild ricing, winter hunting and trapping, and a spring maple syrup camp.
evidence.quote: They show the different activities based on seasons, including summer berry picking, fall wild ricing, winter hunting and trapping, and spring maple syrup camp.

evidence.claim: These are historical representations within a museum devoted to the Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe’s history, culture and contemporary life.
evidence.quote: a museum dedicated to the Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe's history, culture, and contemporary life.

evidence.claim: Other exhibits display contemporary pow-wow outfits and address sovereignty and self-governance.
evidence.quote: "Our Living Culture" displays contemporary Pow-wow outfits.

evidence.claim: address sovereignty and self-governance.
evidence.quote: "Nation Within a Nation" discusses how the Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe have dealt with sovereignty and self-governance rights.

evidence.claim: The present museum opened in 1996, following the original exhibit building’s closure in 1992.
evidence.quote: The original building that these exhibits were placed in was closed in 1992 to make way for the new museum.

evidence.claim: The present museum opened in 1996
evidence.quote: It officially opened to the public on May 18, 1996.

evidence.claim: Exhibits use both English and Ojibwe, and the collections include bandolier bags, moccasins and birch-bark baskets.
evidence.quote: The exhibits show the history of the Ojibwe tribe in Minnesota and incorporates both the English and Ojibwe languages. They feature the artifacts that were collected over the years by the Ayers. The Ayer Collection has 2,200 historical artifacts including bandolier bags, moccasins and birch-bark baskets.

evidence.claim: The Garrison Concourse’s roadside overlook projects 160 feet into Mille Lacs Lake.
evidence.quote: projects 160 feet (49 m) into the lake.

evidence.claim: Its D-shaped platform carries a driveway and parking area, with a curving stone walkway along the edge.
evidence.quote: The principal feature is the overlook, a D-shaped platform with a paved driveway and parking area surrounding a central island, and a curving stone walkway around the periphery.

evidence.claim: Civilian Conservation Corps workers began by building a cofferdam to hold back lake water while they laid the wall’s footings.
evidence.quote: During the summer of 1936 the Civilian Conservation Corps enrollees built a cofferdam to hold back the lakewater and laid the footings of the overlook wall.

evidence.claim: Restoration began in 2011 after ice and waves damaged the wall.
evidence.quote: The Garrison Concourse was extensively restored beginning in 2011.  Ice and wave action had taken a toll on the overlook wall

evidence.claim: Workers recovered several displaced stones from the lakebed and fitted them back into place.
evidence.quote: Several stones knocked out of the overlook wall were recovered from the lakebed and fitted back into place.

evidence.claim: The wall’s granite blocks are roughly finished and laid in an irregular pattern.
evidence.quote: The overlook wall consists of large blocks of granite, roughly finished and laid in a random pattern.

evidence.claim: Stone piers punctuate the wall.
evidence.quote: Three-foot (0.9 m) stone piers are spaced at intervals.
